fields.statement: Built rhiza at fc88da4a into $TMPDIR and ran it by hand in a scratch git repo (rhiza init, change new). A command step 'echo out1; echo boom >&2; exit 3' failed the run and run status --json gave the step detail "exit 3\nout1\nboom". A step printing 'line 1'..'line 500' then exit 1 kept 'exit 1' plus lines 481-500 (21 lines, 186 bytes). A 5000-char single line kept 2048 bytes; 3000 'é' kept a 2046-byte tail starting on a rune boundary. A step that exits 5 silently keeps 'exit 5'; 'nosuchcmd_qa' kept 'exit 127' plus the sh error; a stderr-to-/dev/null step kept only its stdout. A passing step that writes to stdout and stderr kept detail exactly 'exit 0'. go test ./internal/run -run TestCommandDetailKeepsRunnerOutput passed.

With the built binary in a scratch repo, plain rhiza run status after the out workflow failed printed '- b (visit 1): fail, then end: exit 3' then '    out1' and '    boom' indented beneath it; the run start output ends with the same block. The Rex OSC 7501 message rhiza emitted decoded to the single line 'run failed: step "b" ended with outcome "fail"', and run.go's Rex report still cuts detail at its first newline.

With the built binary in a scratch repo, after the out workflow failed at command step b, rhiza inbox printed the failed item, '  step "b" ended with outcome "fail"', then '    exit 3', '    out1', '    boom' indented, then the resume --retry next line; rhiza inbox --json gave detail 'step "b" ended with outcome "fail"
exit 3
out1
boom'. A later run failing on 'nosuchcmd_qa' showed 'exit 127' and the sh error indented the same way.
